issues.title: 2.34.0+: merge_cookies raises "You can only merge into CookieJar" when http.cookiejar is loaded twice
issues.body:
<!-- Summary. -->
In 2.34.0 `RequestsCookieJar` inherits from `http.cookiejar.CookieJar` (imported directly in `cookies.py`), while `merge_cookies` and other checks use `compat.cookielib.CookieJar`.
In 2.33.1 both used `compat.cookielib`. If `http.cookiejar` ends up loaded twice.

This is only reproducable under PyCharms Behave runner.
Works with 2.34.0 with plain behave in a terminal.
Works also with 2.33.1 with PyCharms Behave runner.

## Expected Result

No  "ValueError: You can only merge into CookieJar" using Pycharms behave runner with 2.34.0 or later.

## Actual Result

Running request in combination of Pycharms behave runner following error appears:


```
  File "<project>/adapters/api/rest_client/requests_rest_client.py", line 101, in _request
    prepared: PreparedRequest = self._session.prepare_request(request)
                                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^
  File "<project>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 532, in prepare_request
    merge_cookies(RequestsCookieJar(), self.cookies), cookies
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<project>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/requests/cookies.py", line 614, in merge_cookies
    raise ValueError("You can only merge into CookieJar")
ValueError: You can only merge into CookieJar
```


It seems that the behave runner is loading the package twice.
Ran following code at the failining line inside `prepare_request`:

```
import http.cookiejar, requests.cookies as rc, requests.sessions as rs

jar = RequestsCookieJar()
base = type(jar).__mro__[1]
checked = rc.cookielib.CookieJar

print("RequestsCookieJar same in both modules:", rs.RequestsCookieJar is rc.RequestsCookieJar)
print("base:   ", base, base.__module__, id(base))
print("checked:", checked, checked.__module__, id(checked))
print("stdlib: ", http.cookiejar.CookieJar, id(http.cookiejar.CookieJar))
print("cookielib module:", rc.cookielib, getattr(rc.cookielib, "__file__", None))
```

Output:

```
('RequestsCookieJar same in both modules:', True)
('base:   ', <class 'http.cookiejar.CookieJar'>, 'http.cookiejar', 50096408592)
('checked:', <class 'http.cookiejar.CookieJar'>, 'http.cookiejar', 50100923408)
('stdlib: ', <class 'http.cookiejar.CookieJar'>, 50096408592)
('cookielib module:', <module 'http.cookiejar' from '~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.1-macos-aarch64-none/lib/python3.13/http/cookiejar.py'>, '~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.1-macos-aarch64-none/lib/python3.13/http/cookiejar.py')
```

## Reproduction Steps

Use requests inside a behave project. 
Start a test, which uses the problematic code via the pycharm runner.

##Suggested fix:
Use the same `CookieJar` reference for the base class and the `isinstance` checks (e.g. use `CookieJar` in `merge_cookies`, `cookiejar_from_dict` callers and `RequestsCookieJar.update`, or inherit from `cookielib.CookieJar `again)


## System Information

macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O

issues.title: TestTimeout abandons three delay/10 requests and later tests wait out the server
issues.body:
`TestTimeout` makes three requests to `httpbin("delay/10")` and abandons all of them:

- `tests/test_requests.py:2539`, `test_stream_timeout`, `timeout=2.0`
- `tests/test_requests.py:2573`, `test_read_timeout`, parametrized, `timeout=0.1` (two params)

The client raises at 2.0s and 0.1s, but the pytest-httpbin server keeps sleeping the full 10 seconds and serves requests serially. The next test that needs the server blocks until those sleeps finish.

```
$ pytest "tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods" -p no:randomly
1 passed in 0.56s

$ pytest "tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_read_timeout" \
         "tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods" \
         -p no:randomly --durations=5
19.79s call     tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods
 0.11s call     tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_read_timeout[timeout1]
 0.10s call     tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_read_timeout[timeout0]
3 passed in 20.55s
```

`test_encoded_methods` is one line (`requests.request(b"GET", httpbin("get"))`). The 19.79s is 2 x 10s of server sleep minus the 0.2s the two clients used. In a full run the cost lands on whichever tests happen to follow:

```
19.35s call     TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods
 8.00s call     TestTimeout::test_none_timeout[None]
```

Both call sites need the server to outlast the client timeout, not to sleep for 10 seconds. Lowering the delays leaves the assertions unchanged:

- line 2539, `delay/10` to `delay/3` (client timeout 2.0)
- line 2573, `delay/10` to `delay/1` (client timeout 0.1)

With that change, `TestTimeout` goes from 30.56s to 5.70s and the full suite from 167.44s to 142.04s, with the same results either way: 630 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xpassed. The single failure in both runs is `TestPreparingURLs::test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert`, which is unrelated and fails before the change as well.

Measured at 611c616 on Windows 11, Python 3.14.2, pytest 9.1.1.

issues.title: proxy_bypass_registry uses unanchored re.match (Windows proxy bypass)
issues.body:
This was discussed here multiple times in the past so I'm opening it as a public bug report.

`src/requests/utils.py`, `proxy_bypass_registry` (main, 2.34.2):

```python
if re.match(test, host, re.I):   # start-anchored only
    return True
```

re.match anchors only the start, so ProxyOverride=google.com matches google.com.evil.com and bypasses the proxy for it — an attacker-influenced hostname can escape a proxy meant to inspect traffic.

Diverges from CPython: this is a copy of CPython's old code. CPython now matches with fnmatch (anchored both ends, wildcards preserved). Verified on 3.14:
- `fnmatch("google.com.evil.com", "google.com")` → False (requests returns True)
- `fnmatch("a.example.net", "*.example.net")` → True

Fix: use fnmatch(host, test) to match CPython, or minimally anchor: re.match(test + r"\Z", host, re.I).
issues.author: frenzymadness

comments.author: nateprewitt
comments.body: Thanks for the issue, @frenzymadness. We're already tracking this work for our next release.

comments.author: ege-arhan
comments.body:
Not blocking — I know this is already tracked for the next release, just leaving a tested reference fix in case it's useful.

One-line change in `proxy_bypass_registry`: anchor the converted pattern so a suffix can't escape it:

```diff
- if re.match(test, host, re.I):
+ if re.match(test + r"\Z", host, re.I):
```

Behaviour I verified locally (Windows registry path monkeypatched, Python 3.13):

| override | host | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `google.com` | `google.com.evil.com` | bypassed ❌ | proxied ✅ |
| `internal` | `internal` | bypassed | bypassed ✅ |
| `*.corp` | `a.corp.evil.com` | bypassed ❌ | proxied ✅ |
| `*.corp` | `a.corp` | bypassed | bypassed ✅ |
| `10.0.0.1` | `10.0.0.1x` | bypassed ❌ | proxied ✅ |

Existing exact and wildcard entries keep working because `fnmatch.translate` already emits `\Z` for them; only the plain-entry branch needs the extra anchor.

Branch: https://github.com/ege-arhan/requests/tree/fix/issue-7629 (`e825f8e7` fix + `eb5f5e45` regression tests added to the `test_should_bypass_proxies_win_registry` parametrize block, 5 cases). Happy to close this if the internal patch differs.

comments.author: januththedev
comments.body:
I have a tested fix for this ready, but GitHub is currently refusing to let this account open a pull request against `psf/requests` (`CreatePullRequest` permission denied), so posting the patch here for a maintainer to apply or to let me open.

- branch: [`januththedev/requests:fix/proxy-override-anchor`](https://github.com/januththedev/requests/tree/fix/proxy-override-anchor)
- commit: `7b68766`

## The change

`src/requests/utils.py`:

```diff
             test = test.replace(".", r"\.")  # mask dots
             test = test.replace("*", r".*")  # change glob sequence
             test = test.replace("?", r".")  # change glob char
-            if re.match(test, host, re.I):
+            # The whole host must match. re.match only anchors the start, so
+            # "example.com" would also bypass the proxy for "example.com.evil.net".
+            if re.fullmatch(test, host, re.I):
                 return True
         return False
```

`re.fullmatch` is the smallest change that makes the intent explicit, and it matches what the `no_proxy` path already does — `test_should_bypass_proxies` in `tests/test_utils.py` already covers "does not greedily match domains that merely endswith the no_proxy entry. See CPython bpo-39057", so the registry path was the one left on the old behaviour.

The `<local>` branch above returns before reaching the pattern match, so it is unaffected.

## Tests

Four cases added to the existing `test_should_bypass_proxies_win_registry` table — two that fail before the change, and two controls that already passed:

| URL | ProxyOverride | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `http://example.com.evil.net/` | `example.com` | `False` (was `True`) |
| `http://notexample.com/` | `example.com` | `False` (control, unchanged) |
| `http://www.example.com/` | `*.example.com` | `True` (control: globs still work) |
| `http://www.example.com.evil.net/` | `*.example.com` | `False` (was `True`) |

- Before: `2 failed, 14 passed`.
- After: `16 passed`.
- `pytest tests/test_utils.py` → 232 passed, 1 skipped.
- `ruff check` clean on both files.

The new cases inherit the existing `skipif(os.name != "nt")` guard, since `proxy_bypass_registry` only exists on `win32`.

issues.title: Docstring examples in `from_key_val_list` show the pre-3.12 OrderedDict repr
issues.body:
`src/requests/utils.py`'s `from_key_val_list` docstring shows:

    >>> from_key_val_list([('key', 'val')])
    OrderedDict([('key', 'val')])

Since Python 3.12, `collections.OrderedDict.__repr__` uses the regular dict form ([cpython gh-101446](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/101446)), so on any currently supported Python this actually prints:

    OrderedDict({'key': 'val'})

Reproducer (Python 3.13.5, requests 2.34.2):

```
>>> from requests.utils import from_key_val_list
>>> from_key_val_list([('key', 'val')])
OrderedDict({'key': 'val'})
>>> from_key_val_list({'key': 'val'})
OrderedDict({'key': 'val'})
```

The `ValueError` example in the same docstring is still accurate. Both stale occurrences are on lines 351 and 357, and a grep of the rest of the package found no others.

I have a two-line fix ready on a fork and would be glad to open a pull request if that's welcome. (The compare page says PRs are limited to collaborators, hence this issue.)

issues.body:
Bumps the actions group with 3 updates: [github/codeql-action/init](https://github.com/github/codeql-action), [github/codeql-action/autobuild](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) and [github/codeql-action/analyze](https://github.com/github/codeql-action). Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.37.0 to 4.38.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.38.0

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

v4.37.9

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

v4.37.8

No user facing changes.

v4.37.7

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

v4.37.6

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

v4.37.5

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

v4.37.4

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.2. #4051

v4.37.3

No user facing changes.

v4.37.2

  • The new address format for the config-file input that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 is now enabled by default. In addition to the format described there, the remote= prefix can now be used to explicitly indicate that the input refers to a remote file. All previous input formats continue to be accepted as well. #4023
  • The CodeQL Action can now make use of configured private registries in Default Setup to retrieve CodeQL configuration files from remote repositories that require authentication. This will allow customers to store their CodeQL configuration in a single repository that can then be referenced by Default Setup workflows in other repositories. We expect to roll this and other, related changes out to everyone in July. #4007

v4.37.4

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.2. #4051

v4.37.3

No user facing changes.

v4.37.2

All previous input formats continue to be accepted as well. #4023

This will allow customers to store their CodeQL configuration in a single repository that can then be referenced by Default Setup workflows in other repositories. We expect to roll this and other, related changes out to everyone in July. #4007

v4.37.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019
